National Weather Service Baltimore MD/Washington DC
346 AM EST Fri Nov 6 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
Small Craft Advisories have been issued for Saturday.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- Showers and isolated thunderstorms expected today along and
  east of US-29.

- Turning cooler this weekend with dry weather expected much of
  next week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...

KEY MESSAGE 1...Showers and isolated thunderstorms expected today 
along and east of US-29.

There has been an uptick in shower and thunderstorm activity in
across northern VA and central MD early this morning, especially
in the last hour or so. This activity is moving steadily to the
northeast at 25 to 30 kts east of a slow moving cold front 
located east of the Blue Ridge Mountains. Radar estimates and 
gauge reports indicate hourly rain rates around half inch and as
high as three quarters of an inch in spotty places. Additional
showers and possible thunderstorms are possible further
southeast along increased convergence along the front in a very
moist air mass for early November. While the showers are moving
steadily to the northeast, the showers may exhibit slow 
eastward progression due to mid-upper level flow parallel to the
surface front. By early afternoon, most of the shower/tsra 
activity should be confined to southern Maryland and exit the 
area shortly after 21Z. Turning cooler overnight on 
strengthening NW winds.


KEY MESSAGE 2...Turning cooler this weekend with dry weather 
expected much of next week.

Behind the departing cold front, expect a shift to a dry weather 
pattern for the weekend and into much of next week. Northwesterly 
cold air advection will support falling temperatures on Saturday as 
highs drop into the mid 50s to low 60s (40s to low 50s for the 
mountains). The trailing upper low passes overhead to the north 
which should keep some cloud cover around. Residual gradients also 
support a brisk wind at times with afternoon gusts around 20 to 30 
mph, perhaps nearing 40 mph along the Allegheny Front. Winds remain 
somewhat elevated into Saturday with a chilly night ahead. Forecast 
lows will be in the upper 30s to mid 40s, with spots of low/mid 30s 
around sheltered mountain and river valleys. Any frost generation 
should be limited by the residual winds. High pressure tracks in 
from the middle of the country by Sunday. After a cloudy start along 
the Alleghenies, expect abundant sunshine for the day with highs 
returning to the mid 60s along I-81 and south of I-66 in Virginia. 
This comes with west-northwesterly breezes around 15 to 25 mph. 
Another chilly night lies ahead with widespread lows in the mid 30s 
to low 40s. Some patchy frost is possible where winds turn lighter.

The weather for the work week ahead appears mainly quiet. With the 
upper pattern being amplified, a series of troughs pass by to the 
north of the region. The initial height falls cross the northeastern 
U.S. late Sunday which drags a dry cold front through the area. An 
additional dry system follows suit passing by on Tuesday. The peak 
in the warmth would be on Tuesday before temperatures fall again 
during subsequent days. This would provide additional chances for 
frost and/or freeze as overnight temperatures return to the 30s. By 
late next week, an anomalous upper low settles overhead which may 
support a rather cold period heading into next weekend.

&&

.AVIATION /08Z FRIDAY THROUGH TUESDAY/...

Showers and possible thunderstorms expected through about 16Z,
mainly eastern terminals. Winds shifting to NW later today.

With a dry pattern running for this weekend into early next week, 
VFR conditions are likely at all terminals. Behind a cold front, 
Saturday's northwesterly winds could gust to around 20 to 25 knots 
before dropping to 15 to 20 knots on Sunday. A dry cold front tracks 
in late Sunday which supports additional northwesterly breezes on 
Monday before winds turn more southwesterly on Tuesday.

&&

.MARINE...

An isolated strong thunderstorm is possible across the lower
waters. Strengthening NW winds late tonight into Saturday will
result in solid SCA conditions. SCA's have been issued, which
will probably need to be extended into Sunday morning. 

Behind the cold front, marine winds remain elevated through Sunday 
afternoon which will likely require further Small Craft Advisories. 
A dry cold front moves across the waters late Sunday which supports 
another uptick in the winds for Monday. This should necessitate 
additional advisories for portions of the waters. Gradients weaken 
by Tuesday with gusts falling to around 10 to 15 knots.
